notes:
Summary: Veridian evaluating Dedicated capacity for real-time route-chat and reranking workflows. Primary ask: reserved GPU pool planning across US regions with clear failover headroom and documented throughput guarantees. Key constraints: VPC-only, some workloads must remain in-region for data residency, procurement will require SLA language for latency SLOs and regional uptime.

Customer context: large TMS provider, latency-sensitive routing decisions at edge (warehouse + driver apps). Mixed workload: 1) interactive chat assistant (dispatchers/drivers), 2) reranking for candidate routes, 3) embeddings search for docs and manifests. Heavy peak traffic during EOD batch and morning dispatch windows.

Performance targets discussed: p95 request latency <= 250ms for short chat queries (<=128 tokens), p99 latency target <= 400ms for core route-rerank ops. Sustained throughput baseline: ~4,000 reqs/min, peak burst target: 8,000 reqs/min. Concurrent sessions: target capacity for 550 concurrent chat sessions (avg generation 120-200 tokens), token throughput planning ~600k tokens/hour during peak.

Capacity ask: want reserved GPU pools in us-east-1 and us-west-2. Design preference: active-active with regional weighting (65% primary, 35% secondary) and automated failover. Require headroom calculations: 20% baseline safety + 30% failover buffer when region down. Ask Redwood to provide: GPU type recommendation per model, expected qps per GPU (quantized vs fp16), and projected unit cost with reserved commitment (1yr vs 3yr).

Model strategy: prefer 70B chat-family for dispatch complex prompts (quantized) with automatic fallback to 13B quantized for degraded mode. Embeddings: dedicated smaller TPU/GPU instances. Want kernel selection guidance and suggested batch sizing that respects p95 SLOs.

SLA/Negotiation points: explicit latency SLOs (p95/p99 by route), regional uptime (99.95% per-region & 99.99% overall), credits for SLO misses, transparent routing/fallback docs, and an escape clause to burst to hosted API during sustained outages. Procurement asks for 90-day POC with defined exit criteria (latency/throughput + security sign-off).

Operational concerns & questions:
- Network peering: need exact port/IP list and peering design (infra team).
- Cross-region data residency: which logs are replicated? need retention controls for debug logs.
- Autoscaling: want deterministic reserved pool + burst lanes; clarify how reserved interacts with autoscaler.
- Cost modeling: show per-GPU unit economics incl. egress, storage for KV cache, and burst to hosted pricing.

POC plan (agreed high-level):
- Step 1: Baseline perf on samples (small subset of workloads) using Redwood test harness (week 1).
- Step 2: Two-region load test (us-east-1 + us-west-2) with simulated AZ-failure to validate failover headroom (week 2).
- Step 3: Security review + KMS proofs; sign-off on network peering (week 3).
- Step 4: Final sizing + reserved commitment proposal (week 4).

Quotes & snippets: "If we go active-active we need predictable worst-case headroom — procurement won't accept fuzzy numbers." — Veridian infra lead.

Open items: Redwood to return a detailed "reserved GPU pool per region" spreadsheet (requested 2026-03-01) that shows: GPU type choices, qps estimates, headroom math (20% + 30% failover), and cost for 1yr vs 3yr commitments. Also need sample SLA wording for latency SLOs and credits.

Next tactical: Priya to run initial perf tests against 13B/70B models and produce qps/GPU matrix by 2026-03-09. Jordan to coordinate procurement call with legal by 2026-03-12.
commercial_notes: Looking at enterprise reserved model. Prefers yearly reserved commit but open to 3-year if better unit economics. Wants line-item for burst capacity and explicit pricing for failover traffic.
